title: Plurals
description: Make Swedish nouns plural with -or, -ar, -er, -n or no ending, and say the cars or the houses.

guide.summary: Swedish has five ways to make a plural: -or, -ar, -er, -n and no ending at all, plus a few nouns that change their vowel. You do not have to guess: every noun in your deck carries a note with its definite and plural forms. Learn to read the note, then add -na or -en for the plural with the.

sections.title: Five groups, and the note gives the answer
sections.text: Every noun in your deck has a note such as bilen, bilar: the first word is the noun with the (the definite form), the second is the plural. The ending of the singular is a good clue to the group, but the note always settles it.
steps: Find the noun in the deck and read its note.
The second form in the note is the plural: use it after a number or många.
No note to hand? Use the clues in the next sections: -a words take -or, ett-words in a vowel take -n, ett-words in a consonant take nothing.
watch: A note like Plural only: pengarna means the word is only ever plural (pengar, money).
No plural in a note means you cannot count the word: mjölk, kärlek.

sections.title: -or: en-words ending in -a
sections.text: An en-word that ends in -a drops the a and adds -or. This is the most reliable group.
steps: Is it an en-word ending in -a?
Take off the -a.
Add -or.

examples.en: Two girls are playing in the park.

watch: Ett-words in -a do not belong here: ett öga gives ögon, ett hjärta gives hjärtan.
A few en-words in -a are exceptions: en kollega gives kolleger.

sections.title: -ar: many short en-words and en-words in -e
sections.text: Many one-syllable en-words take -ar. En-words ending in an unstressed -e drop the e first, and words in -el or -er lose the e before the l or r.
steps: Short en-word, or an en-word in unstressed -e, -el or -er? Expect -ar.
Drop a final -e (pojke, pojkar), or the e of -el and -er (nyckel, nycklar).
Add -ar, and check the note when unsure.
watch: Short does not always mean -ar: en katt gives katter. The note decides.
En syster gives systrar: the e drops as in nyckel.

sections.title: -er: words stressed on the last syllable
sections.text: En-words stressed on their last syllable, often borrowed from other languages, take -er. Every word in -tion is in this group, and so are some short words.
steps: Is the stress on the last syllable (te-le-FON, ba-NAN)? Expect -er.
Words in -tion always take -er.
Add -er to the whole word.
watch: A word ending in a stressed vowel also adds -er: en idé, idéer.
Some -er words change their vowel too: en stad gives städer.

sections.title: -n: ett-words ending in a vowel
sections.text: An ett-word that ends in a vowel simply adds -n. Nothing is dropped.
steps: Is it an ett-word?
Does it end in a vowel?
Add -n.
watch: Ett öga and ett öra are irregular: ögon, öron.
Möter is a verb (meets); the plural of möte is möten.

sections.title: No ending: ett-words in a consonant, and words in -are
sections.text: An ett-word that ends in a consonant looks the same in the plural. So do en-words for people that end in -are. The number or a word like många shows that it is plural.
steps: Ett-word ending in a consonant, or an en-word in -are?
Change nothing: the plural is the same word.
Let the number, många or the verb context show the plural.
watch: Do not add -en after a number: tre hus, not tre husen. Husen means the houses.

sections.title: Vowel change: man, män
sections.text: A small group of common nouns changes its vowel in the plural, and most of them also add -er. Learn these as pairs; the note always shows them.
steps: Check the note: does the plural have a different vowel?
Change a to ä or o to ö.
Add -er if the note shows it, doubling k or t where it does.

examples.sv: Jag läser två böcker i veckan.
examples.en: I read two books a week.

watch: Man and män differ only by the dots, so the dots are the whole plural.
Barn looks like it should change, but its plural is just barn.

sections.title: The plural with the: -na and -en
sections.text: To say the cars, the houses and so on, start from the plural and add an ending. A plural in -r adds -na. A plural in -n adds -a. A plural with no ending adds -en. Nouns in -are drop the final e and add -na.
steps: Find the plural first, from the note.
Ends in -r? Add -na. Ends in -n? Add -a.
No ending? Add -en (män doubles the n). Ends in -are? Drop the e and add -na.
watch: Barnen is the written form; in speech many people say barna.
Do not use the form with the after a number: två bilar, not två bilarna.

steps: Check that the noun is an en-word ending in -a.
Drop the -a and add -or.
Short en-word or en-word in -e, -el, -er? Expect -ar, or read the note.
Drop a final -e, or the e of -el and -er.
Add -ar.
Stress on the last syllable, or a word in -tion? Expect -er.
Check the note for short words like katt.
Add -er.
Check that the noun is an ett-word ending in a vowel.
Add -n and nothing else.
Ett-word in a consonant, or a word in -are?
Leave the noun as it is.
Read the note: does the vowel change?
Change a to ä or o to ö.
Add -er if the note has it, doubling k or t where it does.
Find the plural first.
Plural in -r: add -na. In -n: add -a.
No ending: add -en. In -are: drop the e and add -na.

exercises.hint: Väska is an en-word that ends in -a.
exercises.feedback: En-words that end in -a lose the a and take -or.
exercises.explanation: En väska ends in -a, so the a goes and -or comes in: två väskor.

mistakes.why: -ar is the ending for words like bil and pojke. A word in -a swaps its a for -or instead.
Väskan is the bag, one bag with the definite ending. Två needs a plural.

exercises.hint: Drop the final -a first.
exercises.feedback: Blomma follows flicka: en-word in -a, plural in -or.
exercises.explanation: En blomma ends in -a, so the plural drops the a and adds -or: tre blommor.

mistakes.why: -ar does not follow a dropped -a. En-words in -a take the o-ending.
The a must go before the ending is added; keeping it gives two vowels in a row.
After tre the noun must be plural, and blomma is the singular.

exercises.instruction: Replace en with tre (three) and make lampa plural. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Lampa ends in -a.
exercises.feedback: Only the number and the noun change; köper stays the same.
exercises.explanation: En lampa is an en-word in -a, so the plural is lampor: Jag köper tre lampor.

mistakes.why: Lampa ends in -a, and those words take the o-ending, not -ar.
The noun is still singular. Three lamps need a plural ending.
That ending means the lamps. After a number you want the plain plural.

exercises.source: Two women are waiting at the station.
exercises.hint: Kvinna ends in -a.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending of kvinna in the plural.
exercises.explanation: En kvinna ends in -a, so two women is två kvinnor. The verb väntar never changes for plural.

mistakes.why: Kvinna is an en-word in -a, which takes the o-ending, not -ar.
Kvinna is singular; two women need the plural form.
You wait at a station with på, not i.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: We need four girls. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: Flicka ends in -a.
exercises.feedback: Pick the tile with the ending that belongs to en-words in -a.
exercises.explanation: En flicka gives flickor: the a goes and -or comes in. Vi behöver fyra flickor.

mistakes.why: That tile has the -ar ending. Flicka ends in -a, so its plural takes the other ending.

exercises.hint: What does skjorta end in?
exercises.feedback: The plural ending is wrong.
exercises.explanation: En skjorta ends in -a, so the plural is skjortor, like flicka and flickor.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: skjorta ends in -a and does not take -ar.
Många needs a plural noun, and skjorta is the singular.

exercises.hint: Bil is a short en-word.
exercises.feedback: Many short en-words take -ar.
exercises.explanation: En bil is a one-syllable en-word, and the deck note bilen, bilar gives the plural: två bilar.

mistakes.why: -er belongs to words like telefon and banan. Bil takes the a-ending, as its note shows.
-or is for en-words that end in -a, and bil does not end in -a.

exercises.hint: Pojke ends in an unstressed -e. What happens to it?
exercises.feedback: Drop the -e, then add the ending.
exercises.explanation: En-words in unstressed -e drop it and take -ar: en pojke, två pojkar.

mistakes.why: The final -e has to go before the ending; keeping it gives pojke plus ar.
-er is the wrong ending for pojke; words in unstressed -e belong with the a-ending.
Tre needs a plural noun.

exercises.hint: Nyckel ends in -el. Something drops out.
exercises.feedback: Words in -el lose the e before the ending.
exercises.explanation: En nyckel takes -ar, and the e before the l falls out: nycklar, just as cykel gives cyklar.

mistakes.why: The e in -el stays only in the singular; with the ending it drops out.
The e does drop, but nyckel takes the a-ending, not -er.

exercises.instruction: Replace en with två (two) and make hund plural. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Hund is a one-syllable en-word, like bil.
exercises.feedback: Swap the article for the number and give hund its plural ending.
exercises.explanation: En hund takes -ar (hunden, hundar), so the sentence becomes Vi har två hundar.

mistakes.why: Hund takes the a-ending, not -er.
After två the noun must be plural.
En means one, so it cannot stand before a plural; replace it with två.

exercises.source: There are five chairs in the kitchen.
answers: Det finns fem stolar i köket.
I köket finns det fem stolar.
exercises.hint: There are is det finns. Stol is like bil.
exercises.feedback: Check the plural of stol.
exercises.explanation: En stol takes -ar: stolen, stolar. Det finns fem stolar i köket.

answers: Det finns fem stoler i köket.
mistakes.why: Stol takes the a-ending, not -er.

answers: Det finns fem stol i köket.
mistakes.why: Five chairs need the plural form.

answers: Det finns fem stolarna i köket.
mistakes.why: Stolarna means the chairs. After a number use the plain plural.

exercises.hint: Cykel ends in -el.
exercises.feedback: The plural ending is right, but one letter should drop out.
exercises.explanation: In words ending in -el the e falls out before -ar: en cykel, två cyklar.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: the e of -el cannot stay before the ending.
The e drops, but the ending stays -ar.

exercises.hint: Telefon is stressed on its last syllable.
exercises.feedback: Words stressed at the end, often borrowed, take -er.
exercises.explanation: Telefon is stressed on -fon, and such words usually take -er: telefonen, telefoner.

mistakes.why: Telefon takes the e-ending; -ar is for words like bil and pojke.
-or is for en-words ending in -a, and telefon ends in n.

exercises.hint: Banan is stressed on its last syllable, like telefon.
exercises.feedback: Same group as telefon and station.
exercises.explanation: En banan is stressed on -nan and takes -er: bananen, bananer.

mistakes.why: Banan is stressed at the end and takes the e-ending, not -ar.
Fyra needs a plural noun.

exercises.hint: Words ending in -tion all go the same way.
exercises.feedback: Every word in -tion takes the same ending.
exercises.explanation: Words in -tion are stressed at the end and always take -er: stationen, stationer.

mistakes.why: No word in -tion takes -ar; they all take -er.
-or is for en-words ending in -a.

exercises.instruction: Replace en with tre (three) and make katt plural. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Katt is short, but check its note: katten, katter.
exercises.feedback: Short words are not always -ar words; the note decides.
exercises.explanation: En katt takes -er (katten, katter), so the sentence becomes Jag har tre katter.

mistakes.why: Katt looks like hund, but its plural takes the e-ending. Check the note.
After tre the noun must be plural.

answers: Vi har tre lektioner i dag.
I dag har vi tre lektioner.
exercises.hint: Lektion ends in -tion.
exercises.feedback: Words in -tion all take the same ending.
exercises.explanation: En lektion ends in -tion, so the plural is lektioner: Vi har tre lektioner idag.

mistakes.why: Words in -tion take the e-ending, not -ar.
Three lessons need the plural form.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: She has two cousins. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: Kusin is stressed on its last syllable.
exercises.feedback: Pick the ending used by telefon and banan.
exercises.explanation: En kusin is stressed on -sin and takes -er: kusinen, kusiner.

mistakes.why: That tile has the a-ending, but kusin takes the e-ending.

exercises.hint: Äpple is an ett-word ending in a vowel.
exercises.feedback: Ett-words in a vowel just add -n.
exercises.explanation: Ett äpple ends in the vowel -e, so the plural only adds -n: äpplen.

mistakes.why: Ett-words that end in a vowel add only -n, not -r.
Ett-words never take -ar; the vowel at the end just gets -n.

exercises.hint: Ämne is an ett-word ending in -e.
exercises.feedback: Same group as äpple.
exercises.explanation: Ett ämne ends in a vowel, so the plural adds -n: fyra ämnen.

mistakes.why: Ett-words in a vowel do not drop the vowel and take -ar; they just add -n.
The ending is -n alone, without an r.
Fyra needs a plural noun.

exercises.instruction: Replace ett with fem (five) and make äpple plural. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.source: Det finns ett äpple på bordet.
answers: Det finns fem äpplen på bordet.
exercises.hint: Add one letter to äpple.
exercises.feedback: Det finns stays the same for one or many.
exercises.explanation: Ett äpple becomes fem äpplen: an ett-word in a vowel adds -n. Det finns works for both singular and plural.

answers: Det finns fem äppler på bordet.
mistakes.why: The ending is -n alone, without an r.

answers: Det finns fem äpple på bordet.
mistakes.why: After fem the noun must be plural.

answers: Det finns fem äpplena på bordet.
mistakes.why: Äpplena means the apples. After a number use the plain plural.

answers: Jag har två möten i morgon.
I morgon har jag två möten.
exercises.hint: Möte is an ett-word ending in -e.
exercises.feedback: Check the plural of möte.
exercises.explanation: Ett möte ends in a vowel, so the plural adds -n: två möten.

mistakes.why: Ett-words in a vowel add -n, not -r.
Ett-words do not take -ar.
Two meetings need the plural form.

exercises.hint: Äpple is an ett-word.
exercises.feedback: The plural ending is wrong.
exercises.explanation: Ett äpple ends in a vowel, and ett-words like that add -n: fem äpplen.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: -r is not the ending for an ett-word in a vowel.
Fem needs a plural noun.

exercises.hint: Möte is an ett-word ending in a vowel.
exercises.feedback: Treat it like äpple.
exercises.explanation: Ett möte ends in -e, so the plural adds -n: möten.

mistakes.why: Möter is a verb form (meets), not the plural of the noun.
Ett-words do not take -ar.

exercises.hint: Barn is an ett-word ending in a consonant.
exercises.feedback: Ett-words that end in a consonant do not change.
exercises.explanation: Ett barn ends in a consonant, so the plural looks the same: tre barn. The note barnet, barn shows it.

mistakes.why: Ett-words never take -ar.
Ett-words in a consonant take no ending at all.

exercises.hint: Hus is an ett-word ending in a consonant.
exercises.feedback: Sometimes the plural is the same word.
exercises.explanation: Ett hus ends in a consonant, so the plural has no ending: många hus.

mistakes.why: Ett-words in a consonant take no ending.
Ett-words in a consonant take no ending, not -er.
Husen means the houses. Många needs the plain plural.

exercises.hint: Words for people in -are do not change.
exercises.feedback: Lärare, läkare and städare stay the same.
exercises.explanation: En-words for people ending in -are have no plural ending: en lärare, två lärare.

mistakes.why: Nouns in -are add nothing in the plural.
Nouns in -are add nothing in the plural.
Lärarna means the teachers. After två use the plain plural.

exercises.instruction: Replace ett with tre (three) and make ord plural. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Ord is an ett-word ending in a consonant.
exercises.feedback: Only the number changes; ord looks the same.
exercises.explanation: Ett ord has no plural ending, so three words is tre ord.

mistakes.why: Orden means the words. After a number use the plain plural.
Ett-words in a consonant take no ending.
This is the original sentence: ett must become tre.

exercises.hint: Rum is an ett-word ending in a consonant.
exercises.feedback: The house is huset; rooms is the same as room.
exercises.explanation: Ett rum ends in a consonant, so the plural is rum: Huset har fyra rum.

mistakes.why: Ett-words in a consonant take no ending.
Rummen means the rooms. After fyra use the plain plural.
The house needs the definite form, huset.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: There are two doctors here. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: Läkare ends in -are, like lärare.
exercises.feedback: Words for people in -are take no ending.
exercises.explanation: En läkare has no plural ending, so two doctors is två läkare.

mistakes.why: That tile adds -er, but nouns in -are add nothing in the plural.

exercises.hint: The plural changes the vowel, not the ending.
exercises.feedback: The dots over the a are the plural here.
exercises.explanation: En man has the plural män: the a turns into ä and nothing is added. The note mannen, män shows it.

mistakes.why: Man without dots is the singular. The plural is shown only by the changed vowel.
Man takes no ending; its plural is made by changing the vowel.

exercises.hint: Only the vowel changes.
exercises.feedback: Without the dots it is still the singular.
exercises.explanation: The plural of en man is män: a becomes ä. Writing the a without dots gives the singular back.

mistakes.why: That is the singular. The dots over the vowel are the whole plural.
Man takes no ending; its plural only changes the vowel.

exercises.hint: O changes to ö, and the k doubles.
exercises.feedback: Bok changes its vowel and adds -er.
exercises.explanation: En bok gives böcker: o becomes ö, k becomes ck, and -er is added. The note boken, böcker shows it.

mistakes.why: Bok does not take -ar; its vowel changes and it takes -er.
The vowel and ending are right, but the k doubles to ck before -er.

exercises.hint: O becomes ö, the t doubles, and -er comes at the end.
exercises.feedback: Fot changes like bok.
exercises.explanation: En fot gives fötter: o becomes ö, t becomes tt, and -er is added.

mistakes.why: Fot does not take -ar; it changes its vowel and takes -er.
The vowel and ending are right, but the t doubles before -er.
The ending is right, but the o must also turn into ö.

exercises.hint: Hand changes its vowel in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Both the vowel and the ending are wrong.
exercises.explanation: En hand gives händer: a becomes ä and -er is added, like tand and tänder.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: hand does not take -ar.
The ending is right, but the a must turn into ä.

exercises.source: I have two sons and a daughter.
answers: Jag har två söner och en dotter.
exercises.hint: Son changes o to ö in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Look at the plural of son.
exercises.explanation: En son gives söner: o becomes ö and -er is added. The note sonen, söner shows it.

answers: Jag har två sonar och en dotter.
mistakes.why: Son does not take -ar; it changes its vowel and takes -er.

answers: Jag har två soner och en dotter.
mistakes.why: The ending is right, but the o must turn into ö.

exercises.hint: Start from the plural bilar.
exercises.feedback: Take the plural and add the ending for the.
exercises.explanation: The plural is bilar; plurals in -r add -na for the: bilarna.

mistakes.why: Bilar means cars, any cars. The question asks about the cars.
Bilen is the car, just one.

exercises.instruction: Write barn as the children (definite plural).
exercises.hint: Barn has no plural ending. What does it add for the?
exercises.feedback: Plurals without an ending add -en.
exercises.explanation: The plural is barn, which has no ending, so the children is barnen.

mistakes.why: Barnet is the child, just one.
Barna is heard in speech, but the written form adds -en.
Barn has no -ar plural, so there is no -arna form.

exercises.instruction: Make huset plural (the houses). Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: The plural of hus is hus. What does it add for the?
exercises.feedback: Plurals with no ending add -en.
exercises.explanation: Hus has no plural ending, so the houses is husen.

mistakes.why: Plurals in -r add -na, but hus has no ending and adds -en only.
Hus is houses, but not the houses.
This is the original sentence, with one house.

exercises.hint: Start from the plural män and add -en.
exercises.feedback: The n doubles before -en.
exercises.explanation: The plural is män, and it adds -en for the, doubling the n: männen.

mistakes.why: Mannen without dots is the man, just one.
Män has no -er ending, so -na cannot be added.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: The books are on the table. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.source: The books are on the table.
exercises.hint: Start from the plural böcker.
exercises.feedback: Plurals in -r add -na for the.
exercises.explanation: The plural is böcker, and plurals in -r add -na: böckerna. Books lie on a table, so Swedish uses ligger.

mistakes.why: That tile builds on a plural bokar, but the plural of bok is böcker.

exercises.hint: The plural of lärare is lärare. What happens to the last -e before -na?
exercises.feedback: Nouns in -are drop the final -e and add -na.
exercises.explanation: Lärare has no plural ending; for the teachers the final e drops and -na is added: lärarna.

mistakes.why: This is the sentence unchanged: lärare has no -er plural, so there is no -erna.
The final e of lärare drops before the ending; it does not stay in front of -na.
